examples.en: The baby eats baby food, working its mouth.
The hamster nibbles on a sunflower seed.
Grandmother said something, moving her lips.
The child put candy in its mouth and rolled it around.
The way the rabbit nibbles on grass is cute.

examples.ko: 입안에서 오물거리지 말고 크게 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't mumble in your mouth; speak up.

explain: 작은 입을 계속 움직이며 씹거나 말할 때 써서 귀엽고 작은 느낌이 있어요. '우물거리다'도 비슷하지만 더 크고 불분명하게 움직이는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The baby keeps moving its little mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입을'과 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation, with 'mouth'.

phrases.en: The rabbit eats grass, nibbling away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형이라서 먹는 모습을 자세히 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connective form, to describe the way something is eaten.

phrases.en: The baby moves the baby food around in its mouth, chewing in small movements.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입안에 있는 음식을 작은 입으로 계속 굴리며 씹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for chewing food by working it around in a small mouth.
phrases.en_equiv: munch food around in the mouth

explain_en: It is used when a small mouth keeps moving as it chews or talks, with a cute, small feel. '우물거리다' is similar but feels bigger and less clear.

t90.ax: Don't mumble in your mouth; speak up.

examples.en: After a good rest, I got my energy back.
After taking a tonic, my vitality recovered a lot.
My grandmother is still full of vigor.

examples.ko: 몸살을 앓고 나서 원기도 없고 입맛도 없어요.
examples.en: After being sick with body aches, I have no energy and no appetite.
I heard this food is good for restoring vitality.
The children greeted us in voices full of energy.

explain: 몸의 기운을 말해서 아프거나 지친 뒤 회복하는 이야기, 나이 드신 분의 건강 이야기에 잘 나와요. '원기를 회복하다', '원기 왕성하다'처럼 짝으로 익혀 두세요. 평소 말에서는 '기운'이라고 더 많이 해요.

phrases.en: After resting a few days, I got my energy back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지치거나 아픈 뒤에 기운을 되찾는다는 뜻의 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard phrase for regaining strength after being tired or ill.

phrases.en: My grandfather is over eighty but full of vitality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 드신 분이 건강하고 기운찰 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for an elderly person who is healthy and lively.

phrases.en: I got my energy back after eating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '원기'보다 '기운'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, 기운 is used more than 원기.

explain_en: It refers to physical energy and often comes up when talking about recovering after illness or fatigue, or about the health of elderly people. Learn it in set pairs like '원기를 회복하다' and '원기 왕성하다'. In everyday speech people more often say '기운'.

t90.ax: My grandmother is still full of vigor.

en: manic depressive disorder; manic depression; bipolar disorder

examples.ko: 그는 조울증 진단을 받고 꾸준히 치료받고 있어요.
examples.en: He was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and is getting steady treatment.

examples.ko: 조울증 때문에 약을 먹는 친구를 이해해 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to understand my friend who takes medication for bipolar disorder.

examples.ko: 조울증이 있어도 규칙적인 생활이 도움이 된대요.
examples.en: They say a regular routine helps even if you have bipolar disorder.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 조울증에 대해 자세히 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor explained bipolar disorder to me in detail.

examples.ko: 조울증을 앓는 사람들에게는 가족의 지지가 중요해요.
examples.en: Family support is important for people living with bipolar disorder.

examples.ko: 드라마 주인공이 조울증으로 힘들어하는 모습이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The drama showed the main character struggling with bipolar disorder.

explain: 의학 용어라서 병원, 뉴스, 건강 이야기에서 쓰고, 요즘은 '양극성 장애'라는 말도 같이 써요. 기분이 오르락내리락하는 사람을 놀리듯 '너 조울증이야?'라고 가볍게 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 그는 십 대 때 조울증에 걸렸지만 지금은 치료를 잘 받고 있어요.
phrases.en: He developed bipolar disorder as a teenager, but he is getting good treatment now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸렸다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말로, 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for saying someone has come down with an illness, used in medical or health contexts.

phrases.en: These days, manic depression is also called bipolar disorder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 병을 가리키는 의학 용어로, 요즘 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medical term for the same illness, increasingly common today.

phrases.example: 조울증 치료는 약과 상담을 함께 해요.
phrases.en: Treatment for bipolar disorder combines medication and counseling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원과 건강 정보에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase commonly seen in hospitals and health information.

explain_en: It is a medical term used in hospitals, news and health talk, and '양극성 장애' is also used these days. Casually teasing someone with a mood swing by saying '너 조울증이야?' can be rude.

examples.ko: 최면에 걸린 사람은 시키는 대로 행동하기도 해요.
examples.en: A person under hypnosis sometimes acts as told.

examples.ko: 그는 최면 치료로 불안한 마음을 다스렸어요.
examples.en: He calmed his anxiety with hypnotherapy.
I talked myself into doing my homework.

examples.ko: 최면이 풀리자 그는 아무것도 기억하지 못했어요.
examples.en: When the hypnosis wore off, he couldn't remember anything.
Hypnosis is also a field studied scientifically.

examples.ko: 최면에서 깨어난 사람은 졸린 듯 눈을 비볐어요.
examples.en: The person who woke from hypnosis rubbed his eyes as if sleepy.

explain: '최면을 걸다', '최면에 걸리다', '최면이 풀리다'처럼 동사와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 실제 최면뿐 아니라 '자기 최면'처럼 스스로 그렇다고 믿으려 할 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 비유로 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 이번에는 잘할 수 있다고 스스로에게 최면을 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I talked myself into believing I could do well this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 최면이 아니라 마음속으로 계속 그렇다고 믿으려 하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It isn't real hypnosis; it means repeatedly trying to make yourself believe something.
phrases.en_equiv: talk oneself into it; psych oneself up

explain_en: It is often used with verbs, as in '최면을 걸다', '최면에 걸리다' and '최면이 풀리다'. Besides real hypnosis, it is used for trying to make yourself believe something, as in '자기 최면'. In daily conversation you hear the figurative use more often.

examples.ko: 임신 오 개월쯤 되니 태동이 느껴져요.
examples.en: At about five months of pregnancy, I can feel the baby moving.

examples.ko: 처음 태동을 느꼈을 때 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried when I felt the baby move for the first time.

examples.ko: 아기 태동은 사람마다 느끼는 시기가 달라요.
examples.en: The time when you feel the baby move differs from person to person.
The baby's movements kept waking me up at dawn.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 태동 검사를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor did a fetal movement test for me.
I was startled by a sudden kick and called my husband.

explain: 배 속의 아기가 움직이는 것을 말해요. 임신과 병원 이야기에서 '태동이 느껴지다', '태동 검사'처럼 써요. 글에서는 새로운 움직임이나 시대가 막 시작되는 것을 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I feel the baby's movements every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 임신한 사람이 배 속 아기의 움직임을 느낄 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say a pregnant person feels the baby move.

phrases.en: I had a fetal movement test at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 잘 움직이는지 보는 병원 검사를 말할 때 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The set phrase for the hospital test that checks the baby's movement.

phrases.example: 요즘 아기가 태동이 활발해서 잠을 잘 못 자요.
phrases.en: The baby moves a lot these days, so I can't sleep well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 자주, 힘차게 움직일 때 형용사 '활발하다'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the adjective '활발하다' when the baby moves often and strongly.

explain_en: It means the movement of the baby in the womb. It is used in pregnancy and hospital talk, as in '태동이 느껴지다' or '태동 검사'. In writing it is also used figuratively for a new movement or era just beginning to stir.

examples.en: These pants are loose around the waist, so they're comfortable.
I stayed home wearing a baggy T-shirt.

examples.ko: 이 치마 입으면 엉덩이가 펑퍼짐해 보이지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't my hip look wide when I wear this skirt?
That dress is too baggy.
As I got older, my figure became broader and rounder.

examples.ko: 옷을 펑퍼짐하게 입으면 더 커 보여요.
examples.en: If you wear baggy clothes, you look bigger.

explain: 옷이 헐렁하고 넉넉할 때, 또 엉덩이나 몸이 옆으로 넓고 둥글게 퍼져 있을 때 써요. 사람의 몸에 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니 남에게는 조심해서 말해요.

phrases.en: I wore the shirt loose and roomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 옷을 넉넉하게 입는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, it describes wearing clothes loosely.

phrases.en: The pants are loose.
phrases.nuance_ko: '펑퍼짐하다'보다 옷이 몸에 맞지 않고 크다는 느낌이 강하고 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 펑퍼짐하다, with a stronger sense that the clothes are too big.

phrases.example: 이 옷은 펑퍼짐하지 않아서 몸에 잘 맞아요.
phrases.en: This outfit isn't baggy, so it fits well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 옷이 넓지 않고 몸에 맞는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says clothes aren't baggy and fit the body.

explain_en: It describes clothes that are loose and roomy, or a body or hips that spread wide and round. Using it about someone's body can be rude, so be careful when talking about other people.

en: to be weak; to be fragile; to be feeble

examples.en: I was physically frail as a child.
Grandma has become frail these days.
Sometimes people give herbal tonic to a frail child.
My stamina is weak, so it's hard to walk for long.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 수비가 허약해서 자주 져요.
examples.en: That team's defense is weak, so they lose often.

examples.ko: 허약하지 않으려면 운동을 꾸준히 해야 해요.
examples.en: To not be frail, you need to exercise steadily.

explain: 사람의 몸이 약해 쉽게 아플 때 써요. '약하다'보다 체질이 원래 약하다는 느낌이 강해서 건강 이야기에 어울려요. 팀의 수비처럼 힘이 부족한 조직에 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A frail child catches colds often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 '-ㄴ' 형태로 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form describes a person before a noun.

phrases.en: My grandfather is not frail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 약하지 않다고 부정형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says someone's body is not weak.

phrases.en: I have a weak constitution, so I get sick often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 원래 약한 타입을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who is naturally weak in body type.

explain_en: It describes a body that is weak and gets sick easily. It feels more constitutional than 약하다, so it fits health talk. It can also be used figuratively for an organization lacking strength, like a team's defense.

t90.ax: I was physically frail as a child.

examples.en: You look really healthy and rosy today.
I was so shocked that the color drained from my face.
Your complexion is poor and you look low on energy.
My mom checked my complexion first.

examples.ko: 혈색이 돌아온 걸 보니 다 나았나 봐요.
examples.en: Your color is back, so you must have recovered.
Just having good color makes you look much healthier.

explain: 얼굴빛이 건강해 보이는지를 말할 때 써서 '혈색이 좋다/나쁘다/돌다'가 가장 흔해요. 일상에서는 '얼굴빛'이나 '안색'이라고도 하는데, '안색'은 기분이나 건강 상태가 드러난 표정까지 포함해요.

phrases.example: 따뜻한 차를 마시자 얼굴에 혈색이 돌았어요.
phrases.en: After I drank warm tea, color came back to my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창백하던 얼굴에 생기가 돌아올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when color and life return to a pale face.

phrases.example: 요즘 혈색이 안 좋아 보여요. 병원에 가 보세요.
phrases.en: You don't look well lately. Please see a doctor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강이 안 좋아 보인다고 걱정하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when worrying that someone looks unhealthy.

phrases.en: You look pale. Are you okay?
phrases.nuance_ko: 혈색보다 일상에서 더 자주 쓰고, 기분이나 표정까지 포함해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily speech than 혈색, and it also covers mood and expression.

explain_en: It describes whether your face looks healthy, most commonly as '혈색이 좋다/나쁘다/돌다'. In daily talk people also say '얼굴빛' or '안색', and '안색' also includes the look that shows mood or health.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 환각을 본 것 같아요.
examples.en: I was so tired that I think I saw things that weren't there.

examples.ko: 오래 굶으면 환각이 보이기도 한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that if you go hungry for a long time, you can even see hallucinations.
That moment felt like a dream or a hallucination.

examples.ko: 열이 너무 높아서 환각 증상까지 나타났어요.
examples.en: The fever was so high that even hallucination symptoms appeared.

examples.ko: 인공지능이 없는 사실을 말하는 것을 환각이라고 불러요.
examples.en: When AI states facts that don't exist, it is called a hallucination.

examples.ko: 사막에서 물이 보이는 환각에 빠진 사람 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about a person who fell into a hallucination of seeing water in the desert.

explain: '착각'은 잘못 생각하는 것이고, '환각'은 실제로 없는 것이 보이거나 들리는 것처럼 느껴지는 거예요. 요즘은 AI가 없는 정보를 지어내는 것도 '환각'이라고 해요. '환각을 보다', '환각에 빠지다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Hallucination symptoms appeared after I took the medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 약 때문에 없는 것이 보이거나 들리는 증상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for symptoms of seeing or hearing things that are not there, caused by illness or medicine.

phrases.en: He was lost in hallucinations for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환각이 계속되는 상태에 들어갔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means falling into a state where hallucinations continue.

phrases.en: I was so tired that I heard things that were not there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환각 중에서 없는 소리가 들리는 것만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The kind of hallucination where you hear sounds that are not there.

explain_en: '착각' is a mistaken idea, while '환각' is when you see or hear something that isn't really there. Nowadays it is also used for AI making up information that doesn't exist. It is used as '환각을 보다' and '환각에 빠지다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling always sleeps in on weekends.
That shop always has lots of customers.
My father is always singing the same song.

examples.ko: 요즘 노상 비가 와서 빨래가 안 말라요.
examples.en: It rains all the time these days, so the laundry will not dry.

examples.ko: 내 친구는 노상 지갑을 잃어버려서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: My friend is always losing his wallet, and I am worried.
As always, I missed the bus again today.

explain: '늘, 항상, 맨날'과 비슷한데 말투가 더 구어적이고, 불만이나 한숨이 섞일 때가 많아요. 길 위라는 뜻의 '노상'(노상 주차)은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: That friend always has a smiling face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불만 없이 중립적으로 쓸 수 있는 가장 평범한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plainest neutral word, without any hint of complaint.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is always on the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노상'처럼 구어적이고 불평하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Colloquial and a bit complaining, like 노상.

phrases.example: 아빠는 노상 바빠서 얼굴 보기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: Dad is always busy, so it's hard to see him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노상' 뒤에 상태를 붙이면 늘 그렇다는 불만이 담겨요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a state after 노상 adds a complaint that it's always that way.

explain_en: It is similar to '늘', '항상' and '맨날', but it sounds more colloquial and often carries a tone of complaint or a sigh. The '노상' meaning 'on the road' (as in '노상 주차') is a different word.

p.n: 노상 is more colloquial and often hints at a complaint about a habit.

t90.ax: That shop always has lots of customers.

en: to be best; to be supreme

examples.ko: 오늘은 날씨가 더없이 좋아서 점심을 공원에서 먹었어요.
examples.en: The weather was so perfect today that I ate lunch in the park.

examples.ko: 이 집은 조용해서 공부하기에 더없이 좋은 곳이에요.
examples.en: This house is quiet, so it is the best place to study.
A child's smile is the greatest joy to parents.

examples.ko: 이렇게 맛있는 음식을 먹다니 더없이 행복해요.
examples.en: I am supremely happy to eat such delicious food.
The exam is over, so my heart feels incredibly light.
I was extremely grateful that my friend helped me.

explain: '더없이 좋다, 더없이 행복하다'처럼 좋은 뜻의 말과 함께 자주 써요. '더없는 행복'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미기도 해요. '아주'보다 조금 글 같은 느낌이라 말할 때는 '정말, 너무'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'm supremely happy when I'm with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행복이 가장 크다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Conveys that the happiness is the greatest possible.

phrases.en: My child's smile is the greatest joy to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '더없는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 더없는 to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: My friends are extremely precious to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 매우 귀하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a person or thing is extremely precious.

explain_en: It is often used with positive words, as in '더없이 좋다' and '더없이 행복하다'. It can also modify a noun, as in '더없는 행복'. It feels a little more written than '아주', and in speech people also say '정말' or '너무'.

examples.ko: 먼동이 틀 때까지 친구와 이야기를 나눴어요.
examples.en: I talked with my friend until dawn broke.

examples.ko: 먼동 트는 새벽에 일어나 산길을 올랐어요.
examples.en: I got up at the break of dawn and climbed the mountain path.
I got up early to watch the first light of dawn at the beach.
The sea around daybreak was unusually calm.

examples.ko: 먼동이 터 오는 걸 보고서야 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: I only fell asleep after seeing the dawn begin to break.

examples.ko: 새해 먼동을 맞으러 가족과 함께 산에 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the mountain with my family to greet the first dawn of the new year.

explain: 거의 '먼동이 트다'처럼 '트다'와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '새벽', '동이 트다'라고 말하는 경우가 많고, '먼동'은 글이나 노래, 소설에서 분위기를 살릴 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: When the dawn broke, the sea turned red.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 이 짝말로 쓰고, 글에서 분위기를 살릴 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost always used in this pairing, good for setting a mood in writing.

phrases.example: 먼동이 틀 무렵 우리는 산 정상에 도착했어요.
phrases.en: We arrived at the mountaintop around daybreak.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무렵'을 붙이면 그때쯤이라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '무렵' means around that time.

phrases.en: We set out before dawn broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '먼동이 트다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than '먼동이 트다' in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It almost always appears with '트다', as in '먼동이 트다'. In daily talk people often say '새벽' or '동이 트다' instead, while '먼동' suits writing, songs and novels where you want to set a mood.

examples.en: Election day is close, so the candidates are very busy.

examples.ko: 마감이 박두했는데 아직 반도 못 썼어요.
examples.en: The deadline is right around the corner and I haven't even written half.
When exams are imminent, there are no seats in the library.

examples.ko: 새 영화 개봉이 박두해서 벌써 기대돼요.
examples.en: The new movie's release is near, so I'm already excited.
The news says the day of the decisive match is near.
The closer a crisis gets, the calmer you need to be.

explain: 날짜나 사건이 바로 코앞에 닥쳤을 때 쓰는 글말투예요. 일상 대화에서는 '다가오다'나 '코앞이다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 주로 선거, 마감, 개봉처럼 정해진 날이 있는 일과 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 마감이 박두한 때라 사무실이 아주 조용해요.
phrases.en: The deadline is imminent, so the office is very quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '코앞에 닥친 ~'라는 뜻으로 쓰는 글말투 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal, written-style modifier form meaning 'imminent', placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The exam is getting close, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박두하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same idea as '박두하다', but a much easier word used in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The deadline is right around the corner, so I have no time to rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 가까이 닥쳤다는 느낌을 구어체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A colloquial way to say something is just about to happen.

explain_en: This is a formal, written-style word for when a date or event is right around the corner. In daily talk people often say '다가오다' or '코앞이다' instead. It mostly goes with things that have a set date, such as elections, deadlines and releases.

examples.en: The district office came for a surprise safety inspection.
It was an unexpected visit, so the house was a mess.

examples.ko: 학교에서 불시 소지품 검사를 해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised when the school did a surprise check of our belongings.

examples.ko: 불시에 정전이 되어서 작업하던 파일을 잃었어요.
examples.en: The power suddenly went out and I lost the file I was working on.

examples.ko: 불시 소방 훈련이라 모두 서둘러 밖으로 나갔어요.
examples.en: It was a surprise fire drill, so everyone hurried outside.

examples.ko: 불시에 닥친 일이라 대응하기가 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: It came up out of the blue, so it wasn't easy to respond.

explain: '갑자기'가 상황이 확 변한다는 느낌이라면, '불시'는 예상하지 못한 때라는 점이 중심이에요. '불시에'로 쓰거나 '불시 점검', '불시 검사'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 점검이나 방문이 미리 알리지 않고 이루어질 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: A surprise hygiene inspection came to the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 알리지 않고 갑자기 하는 점검을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an inspection done suddenly without advance notice.

phrases.en: A guest showed up unexpectedly and I was very surprised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 말도 없이 예상 못 한 때에 온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone comes at an unexpected time without telling you first.

phrases.en: I was very surprised by the unannounced visit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-의'를 붙여 예고 없이 갑자기 온 방문을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-의', it describes a visit that comes with no warning.

explain_en: While '갑자기' stresses a sudden change, '불시' focuses on an unexpected time. It is used as '불시에' or before other nouns, as in '불시 점검' and '불시 검사', for inspections or visits made without advance notice.
